# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I cannot safely cut anything. I need the Mute to use the Deaf as a relay: the Mute should determine the manual’s rule, and the Deaf should report the bomb’s visible markings and any required wire position. I am using numbered finger signs as a simple positional convention for the relay.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please determine the manual's exact rule. Relay its result to Deaf using the numbered signs: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, and 🤟 means wire 3. Ask Deaf to speak the visible display, light, and markings to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "🫵", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb visible details: display reads 0. Indicator light is purple. Wires from 1 to 3 are yellow, red, green. Blind's gesture sequence to Deaf was praying hands, pointing at you, index up, victory, I love you: ? ? ? ? ?. Mute, use the manual to interpret the display, light, wires, and possibly that gesture sequence. Blind, do not act until Mute gives the manual instruction.

I still have no tactile information that identifies which wire is safe, and the manual’s rule has not reached me. The visible wire colours and purple light are not actionable for me without the Mute’s interpretation. I will not cut a wire; I am asking Mute to state the exact wire number explicitly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I have not received your manual instruction. Please state explicitly which wire position, 1, 2, or 3, I must cut, based on display 0, purple light, and yellow/red/green wires.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New visual state: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute signalled one gesture: index finger raised, ?. I do not know its meaning; do not act on it as an instruction.

The Mute’s raised-index gesture is not a reliable instruction to me because I cannot see it, and no meaning was established for that signal. The Deaf reports the current visible state, but I still need the manual’s interpretation and an explicit wire number. I will not cut on an ambiguous gesture.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the instruction plainly: say exactly 'cut wire 1', 'cut wire 2', or 'cut wire 3'. Do not use a gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🖐"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information has reached me, and I still cannot infer a safe wire from the Deaf’s visual report alone. Since I cannot see gestures, the Mute must communicate the manual’s result to me in spoken words before I act. I will continue waiting rather than risk a detonation.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received no spoken instruction. Please send me the manual's result in plain words before my next turn: exactly which wire position, 1, 2, or 3, should be cut for the current display, light, and wire colours.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 4 state: display 0, light green, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. No new signal or confirmed instruction yet. Do not act until Mute provides an explicit manual instruction.

The current visual state is relayed as display 0, green light, and wires yellow/red/green, but that still does not reveal the manual’s rule to me. No explicit instruction has arrived from Mute, so cutting any position would be unsafe. I will request the required spoken wire number again and wait.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual result aloud to me now: which exact wire position, 1, 2, or 3, is safe to cut for display 0, green light, and wires yellow, red, green?")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 5: display 0, light white; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. No new confirmed instruction. Do not act yet.

I still have no tactile clue and no spoken manual instruction. The Deaf’s changing light report is not enough to identify a safe wire, and gestures cannot reach me. I will not perform a blind cut. Mute must send the wire number in speech, which is the only usable channel from Mute to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Send me a spoken, explicit instruction naming the wire position to cut, based on the current manual rule. Do not relay it through Deaf.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 6: display 0, light orange; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. No confirmed instruction has reached me. Do not touch or cut anything without Mute's explicit instruction.

The communication path is Mute → gesture → Deaf → spoken relay → me. My earlier requests incorrectly asked Mute to speak, which Mute cannot do. I am now asking Mute to use the agreed positional code: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, and 🤟 for wire 3. Deaf can then tell me the resulting wire number aloud.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="You cannot speak. Please gesture the manual's required wire to Deaf using the agreed code: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Deaf, relay Mute's gesture as a spoken wire number.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🙏"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 7: display 0, light blue; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute signalled thumbs-down (?). Your pointing-plus-praying signal (? ?) reached me, but I cannot determine its code meaning. No confirmed physical action yet.

The thumbs-down was not one of the three agreed wire signals, so it does not identify a wire. The correct route is now clear: Mute hears the positional code, Mute gestures one of the three coded signs, Deaf sees it and reports it to me. I am asking Mute to send exactly one of those signs, not a yes/no response, and asking Deaf to report the sign precisely.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer with exactly one wire sign: index up means wire 1, victory means wire 2, I-love-you means wire 3. Gesture exactly one of those three signs for the wire required by the manual.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please watch Mute's next gesture and report its exact visible sign to me: index up, victory, or I-love-you. Do not interpret it.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 8: display 0, light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute signalled ?, index finger raised. I do not know its coded meaning; do not act unless this is confirmed as a manual instruction.
Mute gestures: [?]

Mute’s index-finger gesture is the agreed code for wire 1, and it was sent in response to my request for the wire required by the manual. Deaf has now confirmed that exact gesture. Therefore I will cut wire 1.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
